item.title: DOP FY27-28 AIM Program Contract with GSS
item.description:
Probation | Procurement | Award | $2.1M | Vendor: Good Shepherd Services | Flagged: Contract value ≥ $1M

In accordance with Section 3-04(b)(2)(iii) of the Procurement Policy Board (PPB) Rules, the Department of Probation (DOP) is requesting approval to extend the existing contract with Good Shepherd Services, (GSS) through a Negotiated Acquisition Extension (NAE) to support the continuation of services under the Advocate, Intervene, Mentor (AIM) Program. The contract term is from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2028 in the amount of 2,145,203.52 for this period. 

The AIM Program is an Alternative to Placement (ATP) intervention designed for high-risk, justice-involved youth on probation. The program provides intensive, community-based mentoring through a one-on-one model that pairs participants with paid advocate-mentors who are available around the clock and serve as consistent, trusted supports. Advocate-mentors are credible messengers with strong ties to the communities served and lived experience that enables effective engagement with participants. Over an approximately six- to nine-month, court-mandated period, youth receive individualized support focused on improving decision-making, strengthening family and community connections, and reducing further justice system involveme…

item.title: Comprehensive Services for Immigrants
item.description:
Youth and Community Development | Procurement | Award | $375K | Vendor: Bronxworks Inc | Flagged: Sole-source / non-competitive

Immigrant Family Services: Bronx

DYCD plans to extend their Immigrant Families contracts. These providers deliver comprehensive services for immigrant families living in low income neighborhoods throughout the city of New York. The goal of the comprehensive services to immigrant families is to:  Identify the complex and multiple needs of newly-arrived limited English proficiency families, and, in collaboration with a network of community-based providers, ensure that they gain access to services that help them become self-sufficient and prosper. Help each enrolled family build the self-advocacy skills and gain the knowledge to enable them to address specific challenges and navigate key systems that impact their lives (for example, the education, healthcare, housing, benefits, tax, workplace, and legal and immigration systems).

item.title: NDA Healthy Families NAQ
item.description:
Youth and Community Development | Procurement | Award | $417K | Vendor: Chinese American Planning Council Inc | Flagged: Sole-source / non-competitive

The Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD), as the designated Community Action Agency for New York City, administers the federal Community Services Block Grant (CSBG) program to combat poverty and provide services that empower low-income individuals and families to achieve self-sufficiency. To maximize the impact of CSBG funding, DYCD targets funds to low-income neighborhoods designated as Neighborhood Development Areas (NDAs). The NDA Initiative promotes community-level engagement to ensure that services address the most pressing needs within each community. Programs use a strength-based approach, partnering with participants to build upon existing assets and capacities to achieve personal and community goals. Given the specialized nature of these services and the need for continuity and responsiveness to local community conditions, DYCD seeks approval to use the Negotiated Acquisition method in accordance with PPB Rule §3-04(b)(2)(i)(D). This approach allows the agency to negotiate directly with qualified community-based organizations (CBOs) that have demonstrated experience, trust, and engagement within their respective NDAs.

item.description:
Health and Mental Hygiene | Procurement | Intent to Award | Due: 2026-10-16 | Flagged: Contract value ≥ $1M

Pursuant to PPB Rule 3-04(b)(2)(i)(D), the NYC Health Department intends to process a Negotiated Acquisition solicitation as there is a compelling need for gender-affirming care services that cannot be met timely by competitive sealed proposals. NYC Health will contract with organizations providing or facilitating the provision of gender-affirming care to patients under age 18. This includes the prescription and administration of puberty-blockers and hormone replacement therapy to all minor patients for whom such services are medically necessary based on the prevailing standards of care.
